reason: The upper tract ends beside the colon, so joining them should make the continuous digestive tube the goal asks for.
expectation: I expect the small intestine to connect to the colon in one digestive tract.

alternatives.reason: Placing the eye is also a clear goal, but I chose to complete the gut connection first.

effect: The digestive tract is connected, so the remaining goal is to place the eye and ears.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the small intestine join the colon while food and blood stayed on separate routes.
reason: The eye's optic nerve leads toward the brain, so placing it in the head fits the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the eye to be placed in the head with its optic nerve leading toward the brain.

alternatives.reason: The ears also belong in the head, but I chose to place the eye first.

effect: The eye is in its socket and connected to the brain; the ears still need to be placed.
reaction: The supplied second eye was a small surprise.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it places the ears to complete the head goal.
expectation: I expect the ears to fit into the head with their nerves leading toward the brain.

effect: The ears are in place with their hearing and balance nerves connected to the brain, completing the chapter.
reaction: It was reassuring that the balance sensors stayed part of the same ears rather than being added twice.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the digestive tract was most worthwhile: it showed a continuous food route while absorbed material crosses into blood.

leastWorthwhile.text: Placing the ears was straightforward and the only offered combination, so it involved little decision-making.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the second eye was supplied when I placed the first one.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the goals and pictures made both projects clear.

continue.text: I might continue to see how the assembled parts join the rest of the body, although these placements were fairly predictable.
